topRisks: G4-only ontology sidecar with today's sanitizedToolkit: McpServerClient is absent, CurrentMcpCaller is None, GovernedTierGate fail-closed-refuses every mutation (dead mutation surface).
If mcp-kit keeps reading mcp-session-id after Effect stops minting/validating it, the grant-run key becomes a client-supplied string: new id resets freeze and TTL; a leaked id joins another chain.
OntologyChangeActor already attributes HTTP mutations by per-request clientId, so provenance does not match the session-keyed ledger run even before the protocol flip.
Grant-expired permanence is untested at the gate; never-evict is comment-enforced. Any new key that a client can rotate reintroduces the TTL-reset defect PR 5 already hit.
GovernedEgress remains process-scoped and time-joined; concurrent conversations make that audit join weaker, and a new identity object is the recorded seam to close it.
decisionChallenges: G4 (v2026_07_28-only on every in-repo server) removes initialize, so Effect never mints mcp-session-id; Decision 10's 'transport-assigned session identifier' ceases to exist unless beep-effect mints a replacement.
G4 plus current mcp-kit is fail-closed: no McpServerClient (middleware dies on 2026-07-28) means no CurrentMcpCaller means no governed dispatch.

Keeping a stateful protocol on the ontology sidecar, or a mixed stateful+stateless list, preserves today's session machine and contradicts G4; Effect supports mixed lists with at most one stateless adapter.
Keying on the verified per-launch bearer is G4-compatible but changes Decision 10's substance from 'a run is an MCP session' to 'a run is a sidecar launch'.
grillQuestions: Is 'a run is an MCP conversation' still the invariant once 2026-07-28 has no conversation, and if yes who mints the conversation id without initialize?
Does G4 apply to the ontology sidecar or only to driver MCP servers? Mixed lists and sidecar-stateful-only are implementable Effect options.
Who is allowed to reset grant TTL: any client that can initialize (today), whoever obtains a newly minted token, or only process restart / token rotation?
Must two concurrent conversations on one sidecar have isolated chains, given the gate lock is already process-global because 'the desktop surface has one interactive caller'?
Should OntologyChangeActor stop using clientId so provenance matches the ledger run key?
Is this the moment to give GovernedEgress a session seam, or does it stay process-scoped?
Are driver MCP servers expected to grow GovernedTierGate, or is session identity sidecar-only?
If a signed run token is minted, is the minting event first tools/call, first authenticated HTTP request, or an explicit open-run tool?
Is 'mutations unavailable until identity is replaced' an acceptable ship gate for the protocol flip, or must identity land in the same PR?
